▶Linear-Phase (FIR · bake) ? Designs a symmetric FIR filter from the band magnitudes (RBJ biquad cookbook → cascade → inverse FFT → Hann window) and applies it via overlap-add convolution. Because the filter is symmetric, every frequency experiences the same delay — no phase smear, transients stay sharp.

Trade-off: linear phase introduces pre-ringing (a tiny sinc-like ripple before transients). For most material this is inaudible; for hard-attack percussion it can occasionally soften the click. Use the Parametric (IIR) above if you hear it.

Taps: more taps = sharper bands & better low-frequency resolution but more pre-ring and longer render. 8192 is a good default; 32768 for mastering-level surgery on bass.

▶Tilt + Tone (live) ? One-knob tonal shaping. Tilt rotates the spectrum around Pivot — positive tilt = brighter (highs up, lows down), negative = darker. Body, Warmth, Presence, and Air are macro pushes on a single fixed band each (≈120 Hz / 250 Hz / 3.5 kHz / 12 kHz).

Live, IIR — affects playback in real time, not baked. Stack it with the Parametric for surgical work + tone shaping in one chain.

▶4-Band Tape Expander
Splits into four bands (< 80 Hz · 80 Hz – 3 kHz · 3 – 9 kHz · > 9 kHz) and applies an independent downward expander to each, then sums them. Dolby-A inspired — not a calibrated decoder. Use to tame hiss / floor noise on tape transfers, or to creatively shape per-band dynamics. Threshold = where expansion starts. Ratio = aggressiveness (2:1 mirrors Dolby A). Attack/Release = per-band envelope speed.

▶📏 Loudness Normaliser (LUFS)
Measures integrated loudness (ITU-R BS.1770-4 K-weighted, 400 ms gated) and applies a single gain to hit the target. With Limit on (default), peaks above the ceiling are smoothly tanh-soft-clipped so the target is reached even when the source is already loud. With Limit off, the gain is capped to keep peaks below the ceiling — which means a softer file when the source is already at commercial loudness.

🧠 Auto Denoise — One-Click
Single-click broadband noise reduction. Auto-finds the quietest 0.75 s of the file, learns its mean spectrum as a noise profile, and applies a Wiener mask — equivalent to running Auto · Learn · Apply above in one step. The Smooth knob adds 2-D mask smoothing across time + frequency to suppress musical-noise warble that plain Wiener can leave on broadband hiss.
Strength
50%
Smooth

✂ Declicker
Two-pass detector: large clicks first, then subtle ones. Repairs with cubic Hermite (Catmull-Rom) spline interpolation — no kinks or flat segments. Shift+Click on the waveform to spot-repair a single visible spike.
Sensitivity
50%
🌀 Wow & Flutter ? Detects slow pitch drift in old tape and vinyl transfers and applies micro time-stretches to lock the pitch back to its intended trajectory. Best on material with sustained tonal content (sustained piano, organ, vocals, brass); less reliable on percussion-heavy tracks where there's no clear pitch to track.

Pipeline: STFT pitch tracking on mono mix → smooth long-term to find expected pitch → compute per-frame ratio (actual / expected) → build a variable-rate sample map → linearly-interpolated resample.

Strength dials the correction depth — 100 % fully locks pitch, 50 % halves the wobble, 0 % no change. Smooth sets how slow the "intended" pitch curve is allowed to move — short values follow vibrato and bends, long values only correct true wow. 2 s is a sensible default.
Apply on its own audio first — works best when the file is mostly tonal with audible drift. If the result sounds worse than the original, lower Strength or raise Smooth.
Strength
80%
Smooth
2.0 s
Click Apply to detect drift and correct it.
📐 Declipper
Finds runs of consecutive samples that have been flat-topped at or near full scale and reconstructs the original waveform peak using cubic Hermite interpolation seeded with the boundary slopes — naturally restoring the overshoot the clipper destroyed. Best for over-driven digital recordings, tape transfers pushed too hot, or vintage sources with pinned peaks. Threshold sets where a sample counts as clipped (use ≈ −0.3 dBFS for hard digital clip; raise it for soft analog clip). Max Run caps how long a clipped region can be — longer runs are likely real sustained signal (e.g. a held bass note) and are skipped. After repair the file is auto-attenuated by Headroom dB so the new peaks don't immediately re-clip.
Threshold
−0.30 dBFS

⚡ De-Hum / De-Buzz
Surgically notches mains hum and its harmonic series. Click Auto-Detect to find the fundamental (50 Hz EU/UK/AU/most-of-Asia or 60 Hz US/Canada/parts-of-S.America) by analysing the loudest stationary segment, or pick 50 / 60 manually. Q controls notch sharpness — higher = narrower (less collateral on adjacent frequencies). Harmonics sets how far up the series to notch (electrical hum is rarely just the fundamental — buzz is mostly harmonics 2–8).

↔ Azimuth Correction
Corrects inter-channel timing on stereo sources. A mis-aligned tape head or cartridge shifts one channel a few samples in time, smearing the stereo image. Analyse cross-correlates L vs R (over the current region if one is selected, otherwise a middle window) to suggest the offset. Positive offset delays R; negative delays L. Sub-sample values are interpolated linearly.
Offset
0.0 smp
⏱ Time-Stretch ? Stretches the duration without changing pitch. 0.5× = twice as long; 2× = half as long. Phase-vocoder pipeline: forward STFT (Hann, 75% overlap) → per-bin true-frequency recovery → rigid phase-locking around spectral peaks → transient-detect frame freeze → ISTFT with WOLA.

Varispeed mode locks pitch to speed like a tape machine or turntable: 0.5× = +12 st (octave up), 2× = −12 st (octave down). Math: semitones = −12·log₂(Time).

Quality tips: moderate ratios (0.5×–2×) sound cleanest. Bigger FFT = better frequency resolution and smoother sustained tones, but transients (drum hits, plucks) blur more. 4096 is balanced; 2048 for percussive material; 8192 for sustained tones.

🎵 Pitch-Shift ? Shifts pitch without changing duration. +12 st = up an octave; −12 st = down an octave. Internally: phase-vocoder time-stretches by the pitch ratio, then linearly resamples back to the original length. Resampling len·R → len multiplies all frequencies by R while preserving duration.

Quality tips: ±6 st is the cleanest range. Bigger shifts work but artifacts increase with distance from unison. 4096 is balanced; 2048 for percussive material; 8192 for sustained vocals.

Click any value to type a value (e.g., type 7 for a perfect fifth up).

▶Spectrogram
📊 Spectrogram · 🖌 Spectral Repair ? Long-view time-frequency display + paint-to-repair. Hum shows as horizontal lines (50/60 Hz + harmonics), hiss as a broad bright band across the top, crackle/clicks as bright vertical streaks. Select a region on the master waveform to focus on it; otherwise the full file is shown.

Workflow: 1) Render, 2) 🖌 Brush and drag rectangles around the artifact (drag edges to resize, body to move, right-click to delete), 3) ▶ Audition to hear just the painted band, 4) pick a Mode (Horizontal for time-localised events, Vertical for narrowband tones), 5) Repair. Phase is preserved from the original frame to minimise pre/post-echo.
